questions.question:
Parts of the following sentences have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.
Mr. Prabhakar was first man to arrive at the venue.
questions.solution:
'A)‘was first man' के बदले'was the first man'का use होगा क्योंकि ‘first man’ के पहले definite article ‘the’ का प्रयोग होना आवश्यक है; जैसे— "He was the first person to speak at the meeting."
'was the first man' will be used instead of 'was first man' because before 'first man,' the definite article 'the' is required; Like— "He was the first person to speak at the meeting."

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the errorm from the given options.
Mr. Raghav / brushes his / teeth four / times the day.
questions.solution:
D)‘times the day' के बदले'times a day' का use किया जाएगा क्योंकि सामान्य अभिव्यक्ति में, जब किसी क्रिया की आवृत्ति का जिक्र किया जाता है, तो 'a' का प्रयोग indefinite article के रूप में होता है, जो कि एक सामान्य दिन का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। 'The' एक definite article है, जो किसी विशेष दिन का संकेत देता है, जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं है। उदाहरण: He brushes his teeth four times a day.
'times a day'will be used instead of 'times the day' because, in expressions of frequency, the indefinite article 'a' is used to refer to a typical or general day. 'The' is a definite article that specifies a particular day, which is incorrect in this context.
Example: He brushes his teeth four times a day.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Raveena has made / up her mind to / carried minimum / luggage with her
questions.solution:
D) 'carried' के बदले 'carry' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'to' के बाद हमेशा Verb की base form (मूल रूप) का प्रयोग होता है, न कि Past Tense का। इसलिए सही वाक्य होगा: Raveena has made up her mind to carry minimum luggage with her.
'carry' will be used instead of 'carried' because after 'to,' the base form of the verb is always used, not the Past Tense. Therefore, the correct sentence will be: Raveena has made up her mind to carry minimum luggage with her.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
For the past / three years, / my uncle is /away from home.
questions.solution:
D)is' के बदले'has been'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'For the past' द्वारा दर्शाए गए sentence में कोई ऐसा कार्य हो रहा है जो अतीत से वर्तमान तक जारी है, और ऐसी स्थिति को प्रदर्शित करने के लिए Present Perfect Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है; जैसे— For the past three years, my uncle has been away from home.
'has been'will be used instead of 'is' because the phrase 'For the past' indicates an action that started in the past and continues up to the present, and such a situation is expressed using the Present Perfect Tense; Like— For the past three years, my uncle has been away from home.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
D)'he asked me money'के बदले 'he asked me for money' का use होगा क्योंकि 'ask' के बाद 'for' preposition का प्रयोग आवश्यक है जब 'money' को request किया जाता है; जैसे— He asked me for money to buy a book.

C)'a international'के बदले 'an international' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'international' एक vowel sound से शुरू होता है और vowel sound के पहले 'an' का प्रयोग किया जाता है; जैसे— She studies in an international school.

questions.question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: 1) I will be drive into town later on.
2) I will be driving into town later on.
3) I might drive into town later on.
4) I could be driving into town later on
questions.solution:
A) I will be drive into town later on.
In this sentence, the verb "drive" should be in its present participle form "driving" to match the future continuous tense "will be." The correct sentence should be "I will be driving into town later on."
B. I will be driving into town later on. (Correct – future continuous tense is correctly used.)
C. I might drive into town later on. (Correct – "might" followed by the base form of the verb is correct.)
D. I could be driving into town later on. (Correct – "could be" followed by the present participle form is correct.)

questions.question:
Identify the proper explanation of the error in the given sentence.
Mohan insisted to go there.
options: 1) Error is with the tense. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisting to go there.
2) Error is in the sentence formation. Preposition and gerund are required. The correctsentence should read like this: Mohan insisted on going there.
3) Error is with the verb. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insist to going there.
4) Error is with the preposition. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisted go there
questions.solution:
B) Error is in the sentence formation. Preposition and gerund are required. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisted on going there.
"insist" verb के बाद "on" preposition और उसके बाद gerund (verb + ing) का use किया जाता है। इसलिए, "insisted to go" गलत है और इसे "insisted on going" होना चाहिए।
A. Error is with the tense. (Incorrect – error tense में नहीं है बल्कि sentence formation में है।)
C. Error is with the verb. (Incorrect – "insisted" verb सही है; error preposition और gerund के साथ है।)
D. Error is with the preposition. (Incorrect – sentence formation के लिए preposition "on" और gerund "going" दोनों की आवश्यकता है।)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.
Soldiers in / the Indian Armed Forces are / trained never to / fight cowardly
questions.solution:
D) 'trained never to' के बदले 'never trained to' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए क्योंकि 'never' का स्थान यहाँ गलत है। 'Never' को आमतौर पर मुख्य क्रिया के पहले रखा जाता है ताकि वाक्य की संरचना सही रहे।
Rules of adverb placement
1. Adverbs of frequency (e.g. always, never, often) are usually placed before the main verb in a sentence.
2. Adverbs of manner (e.g. quickly, slowly, carefully) are usually placed after the main verb or after the object of the sentence if there is one. If you want to add emphasis, the adverb of manner might be placed before the main verb.
3. Adverbs of degree (e.g. very, extremely) are always placed before the adjective or adverb they are modifying.
4. Adverbs of time (e.g., now, soon) usually come at the end of sentences or clauses they modify unless they are used to modify an entire sentence or clause in which case they should be placed at the beginning of that sentence or clause for emphasis and clarity.
5. Adverbs that modify adjectives or other adverbs should be placed immediately before them for emphasis and clarity; however, this rule is not absolute, as there may be cases where it makes more sense to place the adverb elsewhere in the sentence.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
Ramesh licked (A) / honey and (B) / said that (C) / it tasted sweetly. (D)4. Aliens
questions.solution:
A) 'tasted sweetly' में error है क्योंकि 'sweetly' adverb है और यहां adjective 'sweet' का उपयोग होना चाहिए। जब taste, smell, feel आदि जैसे sense verbs का उपयोग किया जाता है, तो उसके बाद adjective का use होता है, न कि adverb का। इसलिए, सही sentence होगा 'it tasted sweet'
The error is in 'tasted sweetly' because 'sweetly' is an adverb, and the adjective 'sweet' should be used instead. When sense verbs like taste, smell, feel, etc., are used, they are followed by an adjective, not an adverb. Therefore, the correct sentence should be 'it tasted sweet.'

questions.question:

The error is in 'food greedy' because 'greedy' is an adjective, but it is being used as an adverb. The correct form should be 'greedily,' which is an adverb and modifies the verb 'ate.' Therefore, the correct sentence should be 'ate the food greedily.'
